title: Gadulka (bowed fiddle)
summary: The gadulka is a pear-shaped bowed fiddle of Bulgaria, carved from one piece of pale wood. Three bowed strings run over the bridge and a row of fine sympathetic strings sits under them, each with its own small peg on the side of the neck. It plays quick dance tunes and slow songs.
howToPlay: Three strings run down the neck. Each lane marks a string and the place to stop it.
A bead slides to the spot. Press and bow as it lands.
Quick tunes zigzag between two strings; slow ones stay on one.
Start slow, then raise the speed.
rules: The strings are tuned in fifths and fourths, with a minor third and a fourth on each.
A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
heritageNote: In Bulgaria the gadulka plays for dances and in village bands. Its sympathetic strings give the sound a shimmering ring that stays after the bow lifts.
